### 0.1.4 (2026-11-06) [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-4-2026-11-06)

- Fixed: `pinstripe-baseline` mutes deprecations while it loads the app's autoloader, so an old package in the app no longer prints PHP warnings ahead of the count a script reads (found by the 2026-11-05 proof run; new test in tests/BaselineTest.php).
- Added: a public Proof page (`docs/reference/proof.md`, under Reference): the presets run against 82 Wayne State applications, what held, what the run caught in Pinstripe, and what it does not prove.
- Docs: the install steps say to rerun `composer require` with `-W` when a package the app already locks blocks it; Adopting on an existing app covers errors PHPStan cannot baseline and keeping Pint off bundled third-party code.
- Security: the front-page deploy layer moves to Symfony 7.4.23 (symfony/http-foundation and symfony/yaml advisories, including CVE-2026-118514).
- Changed: the docs, README and front page say the npm package, `@waynestate/pinstripe`, is at 0.1.3 (published); the docs pages' dark mode is now charcoal suiting instead of the green cloth, and wide tables shade the edge they scroll toward.
- Changed: the docs pages wear the front page's look: its header and main menu (Docs marked current), Bodoni titles with the gold chalk line, pattern-piece callouts and pager, the gold Copy pill and the green footer, plus a dark mode cut from the green cloth. The theme lives in `docs/_header.html` and `docs/theme/pinstripe.css`, named by the `theme` key in `docs/docs.json`; the vendored docs builder and kit are synced from Squire's unified builder (theme hook, callouts, copy button and keyboard fixes).
- Added: `min-release-age=3` to the repo `.npmrc` beside the existing `ignore-scripts=true`, with a comment naming the unit (days) and the agreeing Renovate `minimumReleaseAge` rule, so npm waits 3 days before installing a freshly published release and never runs dependency lifecycle scripts; the README gains a "Supply chain" section that explains both settings and tells apps to copy both lines into their own `.npmrc`.
- Changed: `pinstripe-baseline` now requires the app's composer.json to carry `"extra": { "pinstripe": { "legacy": true } }` before it counts or checks a baseline; this is breaking for existing baseline users, who must add the flag, because a baseline is only for apps adopting Pinstripe late and new apps never set it.
- Added: `--composer=<path>` to `pinstripe-baseline count` and `check` (default `composer.json` in the current working directory), so tests and monorepos can point at another composer.json.
- Changed: the ESLint presets (`eslint/javascript.js` and `eslint/typescript.js`) fail lint on every Vue and accessibility finding: rules the plugins' recommended configs report as warnings are raised to errors, so the editor, a local `npm run lint` and CI agree on what fails. Pre-1.0 break: apps that keep the old behavior (those findings as warnings) spread the new `-warn` export instead.
- Added: `eslint/javascript-warn.js` and `eslint/typescript-warn.js`, exported as `@waynestate/pinstripe/eslint/javascript-warn` and `@waynestate/pinstripe/eslint/typescript-warn`, which keep the exact previous behavior (the plugins' plain recommended configs, warnings stay warnings) for apps adopting the stricter presets gradually; `tests/js/presets.test.mjs` gains four tests around a `tests/js/warn-tier` fixture whose only findings (`vue/attributes-order`, `vue/no-v-html`) were warnings before, proving the strict presets report them as errors and the `-warn` presets keep them as warnings.
- Added: a docs site (site/docs/) built by the shared docs builder from docs/, checked in composer ci.
- Added: `eslint-formatter-gitlab` as a dependency and `tests/js/gitlab-formatter.test.mjs`, which lints the bad Vue fixture with the javascript preset, runs the results through ESLint's `gitlab` formatter, and asserts the Code Quality report is a non-empty JSON array whose findings each carry a description, fingerprint, severity and location, so `eslint --format gitlab` shows ESLint findings in GitLab merge requests; the README gains a "Show ESLint findings in the merge request" note for the Vue section.
- Added: `prettier-plugin-blade` (pinned to 3.3.3, no caret) as a dependency and a `*.blade.php` override in `prettier/index.json` (parser `blade`, 4-space tab width), so the Prettier preset formats Blade views; `tests/js/blade.test.mjs` checks a clean and a messy Blade fixture through Prettier's Node API, and the README gains a "Format Blade views" section with the one-time reformat command and an adopting note.
- Changed: Blade files now format with prettier-plugin-blade; the first run rewrites every Blade file (4-space indent, a space after directive names such as `@vite (`, void tags self-closed), so reformat in its own commit.

### 0.1.3 (2026-11-03) [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-3-2026-11-03)

- Added: `docs/adr/0001-phpstan-level-and-baseline-policy.md`, the ADR recording the PHPStan level 8 cut, the baseline policy (generated once for an existing app, never for new code, and only ever shrunk), and the `composer ci` / `composer-ci` pipeline enforcement point, plus a README note that apps adopting Oxlint keep ESLint for `.vue` files because the Vue and accessibility plugins run only in ESLint.
- Changed: the install instructions now include `composer config allow-plugins.phpstan/extension-installer true`, so a non-interactive install works.
- Added: a Node matrix to the `npm-test` jobs on GitLab and GitHub (Node 22, 24 and 26), so the ESLint and Prettier presets are proven on all three majors; the floor stays 22.13.
- Changed: the front-page deploy layer pins HELMET ^0.3, PROCTOR ^0.4 and CREED ^0.1 (lock: HELMET 0.3.0, PROCTOR 0.4.0, CREED 0.1.6).
- Changed: CI pins Preflight 0.1.4 (GitLab component includes and the GitHub reusable workflow tag).
- Added: `tests/fixtures/laravel-vue`, a combined Laravel + Vue fixture with `resources/js` beside `app/`, so one app tree is linted by Pint and PHPStan (PHP side) and ESLint and Prettier (Vue side) on every run; it carries one planted PHP error (`bad/BrokenGreeting.php`) and two planted Vue defects (`resources/js/bad/Broken.vue` missing a `v-for` key, `resources/js/bad/NoAlt.vue` missing an `alt`), and `tests/js/presets.test.mjs` gains five tests for the Vue side.

### 0.1.2 (2026-11-03) [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-2-2026-11-03)

- Added: PHPUnit tests for the PHPStan ignore rules in `phpstan/base.neon`, which run the raw preset against three one-class fixtures in `tests/fixtures/raw-ignores` and prove an `@phpstan-ignore` without a comment fails, an ignore that matches no error fails, and a commented ignore passes.
- Added: PHPUnit tests for Pint's `--format=gitlab` output, which prove the messy `per` fixture becomes a non-empty GitLab Code Quality JSON array and the clean fixture becomes `[]`.
- Added: a "Tool floors" section in the README with the PHP or Node floor of each locked tool, read verbatim from `composer.lock` and `package-lock.json` and checked by `tests/ToolFloorsTest.php`, so a dependency bump fails `composer ci` until the table is re-cut.
- Added: `phpstan/laravel.neon` pins Larastan's `noEnvCallsOutsideOfConfig` rule on, with `tests/fixtures/laravel/src/EnvLeak.php` and `tests/fixtures/laravel/src/ConfigRead.php` proving the Laravel preset reports an `env()` call outside `config/` and accepts a `config()` call there.
- Added: PHPUnit tests for the opt-in strict-types Pint presets, which run the real Pint against clean and missing fixtures for `pint/per-strict.json` and `pint/laravel-strict.json` and assert each strict config declares its preset and the `declare_strict_types` rule.
- Added: `tests/js/prettier.test.mjs`, which runs the Prettier preset through Prettier's Node API on clean and messy JS and Vue fixtures and on the preset's own options, so `npm test` enforces the preset like the ESLint ones.
- Added: PHPUnit tests for `pinstripe-baseline check --against=<git-ref>`, which build a throwaway git repository in a temp dir and assert the count at the ref and the exit codes.
- Added: `npm-test` CI jobs on GitLab and GitHub that run `npm ci` then `npm test` on Node 22, so the ESLint and Prettier presets are covered in CI.
- Changed: the GitHub workflow pins Preflight's reusable workflow by tag (0.1.2) instead of a SHA, as its comment intended.
- Added: agent-ready site (prompt blocks, Markdown twins, llms.txt), from Squire's kit.
- Pinned symfony/mime v7.4.22 in composer.lock, the fixed version for CVE-2026-45070 (PKSA-wtxr-p26d-nn42, GHSA-vqc8-7275-q272), so the audit step of `composer ci` passes.
- Changed: project names written as words except acronyms.
- Changed: the deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.3 (release options can now live in ./.env.squire).
- Changed: the deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.4 (the local .env.squire file is now git-ignored).
- Fixed: stale capability claims in the site and README.
- Added: `tests/PackageVersionTest.php`, which fails `composer ci` when the `version` in `package.json` does not match the newest `## X.Y.Z (date)` heading in `CHANGELOG.md` or, on a tag pipeline, the tag itself, so npm can always publish from the tag; `package.json` is now 0.1.1, the version the 0.1.1 tag shipped without.
- Changed: CI pulls its Docker Hub images through the GitLab Dependency Proxy (the group's CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX), so pipelines no longer hit Docker Hub's anonymous pull limit.
- Changed: `deploy/composer.json` drops `minimum-stability: dev` (every constraint resolves at stable), and the PROCTOR job for `deploy/` in `.gitlab-ci.yml` drops `allow_failure`, since PROCTOR now passes on `deploy/`.
- Changed: docs and package metadata name an internal GitLab as the canonical repository, with git.wayne.edu and GitHub as read-only mirrors, until git.wayne.edu has CI runners.

### 0.1.1 (2026-10-29) [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-1-2026-10-29)

- Fixed the raw and Laravel PHPStan cuts inheriting `reportMaybesInMethodSignatures` and `reportStaticMethodSignatures` from `phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules`, which made them report phpdoc method signature issues they should not; `base.neon` now pins both to false and `strict.neon` keeps them on.
- Pinned the other eight parameters `phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules` forces on: four low-noise ones stay on in every cut, and `checkDynamicProperties`, `reportMaybesInPropertyPhpDocTypes`, `reportWrongPhpDocTypeInVarTag` and `reportNonIntStringArrayKey` are off in `base.neon` and on in `strict.neon`; the README lists each decision.

### 0.1.0 (2026-10-29) [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-0-2026-10-29)

- Added `bin/pinstripe-baseline`, which counts a PHPStan baseline's ignored errors (`count`) and fails when the baseline grows (`check --max=<n>` or `check --against=<git-ref>`), so baselines only shrink.
- Added `phpstan/strict.neon`, an opt-in PHPStan preset for new apps that turns on `phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules`.
- Added `tests/fixtures/per`, a Pint fixture proving the `per` preset is the PER Coding Style.

## Contributing [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#contributing)

This page explains how to build, test and change Pinstripe, and the rules every change must keep.

### Build and test [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#build-and-test)

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Install | `composer install` |
| All PHP checks (what CI runs) | `composer ci` |
| JS preset tests, Windows | `npm ci; npm test` |
| JS preset tests, Linux and macOS | `npm ci && npm test` |

With only Docker:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c6de224f4689e8f80ed5f5edaf0030b6b8b7839a22a2bcb6722ac87d0 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
```

`composer ci` runs `composer validate --strict`, PHPUnit, the agent-ready check (`php bin/agent-ready.php --check`), `composer audit` and the docs check (`php bin/docs-site.php --check`). The PHPUnit suite is the real check: it installs fixture apps and runs Pint, PHPStan and Rector with each preset against planted code, so a preset that stops catching something fails a test. `npm test` (`node --test`) covers the JS presets, and both pipelines run it on Node 22, 24 and 26, so a broken ESLint or Prettier preset fails the build too.

### CI [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#ci)

- **GitLab:** Preflight's `php-test` (PHP 8.3, 8.4, 8.5), `composer-audit`, `proctor` (on `deploy/`) and `a11y` (on `site/`) components, pinned to 0.5.0, plus `composer-ci`, `npm-test` (Node 22, 24 and 26) and `wayneui-copies` jobs.
- **GitHub:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` calls Preflight's reusable workflow (0.5.0) with `composer ci`, and runs `npm ci` then `npm test` in `node:22`, `node:24` and `node:26` containers.
- Green means `composer ci` passed on all three PHP versions and `npm test` passed on Node 22, 24 and 26, on both.

### Changing a preset [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#changing-a-preset)

- A stricter preset breaks consumers' builds. Add the rule with a fixture that proves it, note it in the CHANGELOG, and ship it in a minor version so consumers opt in.
- Keep the "Tested with" versions in the README in step with what the fixtures actually install.
- When PHPStan, Pint, Larastan or Rector release a major version, bump the constraint here first and run the full suite.

### Rules a change must keep [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#rules-a-change-must-keep)

Every preset is enforced by a test that runs the real tool against a fixture, so a preset that stops working fails `composer ci` here instead of failing a developer's app. A preset is **Enforced** when a test asserts both directions: a clean fixture passes, and a deliberately broken one is caught. The PHP presets run under `composer ci` (PHPUnit); the JavaScript presets run under `npm test`. Both run in CI on GitLab and GitHub, so a preset that stops working fails the pipeline before it reaches an app.

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#related)

- [Best practices](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html)
- [Releasing](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/releasing.html)
- [Upgrading](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html)
- [Changelog](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html)

Source: https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/releasing.html

## Releasing [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/releasing.html#releasing)

This page sets out the steps to release Pinstripe, from the CHANGELOG to the npm publish.

1. Move the lines under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` to a new `## X.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)` heading.
2. Set the same version in `package.json`, in the same release commit: `tests/PackageVersionTest.php` fails otherwise.
3. `composer ci` and `npm test` green locally, then both pipelines green for that commit.
4. Run a secrets scan of the history and check that nothing internal is in the tree.
5. Tag `X.Y.Z` (no `v`) on git.wayne.edu. The push mirror carries the tag to GitHub, and Packagist picks it up from there.
6. **npm is published by hand,** after the tag, from a clean checkout of the tagged commit, by an owner of the `@waynestate` npm scope with two-factor auth:
   ```
   npm ci --ignore-scripts
   npm test
   npm pack --dry-run
   npm publish --access public
   ```
   `npm pack --dry-run` should list only `eslint/`, `prettier/`, `LICENSE`, `README.md` and `package.json`. Publishing cannot be undone, so check the version first with `npm view @waynestate/pinstripe version`.
7. A release needs a maintainer's approval. Never move or delete a published tag.

Warning

A release needs a maintainer's approval. Never move or delete a published tag.

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/releasing.html#related)

## Adopting on an existing app [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html#adopting-on-an-existing-app)

Adopt Pinstripe on an existing app by baselining the legacy findings once, then keeping every exception honest.

### Generate the baseline once [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html#generate-the-baseline-once)

Generate a baseline with `phpstan analyse --generate-baseline`, include it in your `phpstan.neon`, and only ever shrink it. New code gets no baseline. A baseline is a tailor's chalk line: it marks the fabric as it is, and every release you take it in, never let it out.

Some errors cannot go into a baseline. PHPStan says `Some errors could not be put into baseline` and the run stays red; on the 2026-11-05 [proof run](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html) these were classes that extend a class PHPStan cannot find, usually because that code lives in a folder outside `paths` or in a nested app with its own `vendor/`. Fix how PHPStan finds the code first (add the folder to `paths`, or to `scanDirectories` when it is not yours), then generate the baseline again.

### Keep Pint off code that is not yours [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html#keep-pint-off-code-that-is-not-yours)

When the app bundles a third-party library in its own tree (a PDF or spreadsheet library copied in years ago), point Pint at your own folders instead of the whole app, for example `pint --test --config vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/per.json src public`. Restyling a library you do not maintain makes every later update of it a conflict, and very large generated files, such as a PDF library's font maps, can keep Pint busy for many minutes.

### Ignore comments must say why [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html#ignore-comments-must-say-why)

Every cut sets `reportIgnoresWithoutComments` and `reportUnmatchedIgnoredErrors`, so the preset reports an `@phpstan-ignore` that has no comment in parentheses and one whose identifier no longer matches an error on that line. The correct form keeps the reason and the exit plan on the same line:

```php
public function name(?string $v): string
{
    // @phpstan-ignore return.type (why this is safe, and the plan to remove it)
    return $v;
}
```

Pinstripe tests all three cases: the bare ignore fails, the unmatched ignore fails, and the commented one passes.

Warning

An ignore without a reason is a pin left in the cushion: nobody remembers why it was there, and it pokes the next tailor.

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html#related)

- [The strict cut](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html)
- [Baselines only shrink](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html)
- [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [Laravel apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html)
- [ADR-0001: PHPStan level 8 and baselines](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/adr/0001-phpstan-level-and-baseline-policy.html)

Source: https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html

## Baselines only shrink [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html#baselines-only-shrink)

Keep a PHPStan baseline from growing by counting it and failing the build the moment it does.

Pinstripe ships `pinstripe-baseline`, one PHP command that runs on every OS, to keep that promise. It reads both the NEON baseline and the PHP format (`phpstan-baseline.php`).

### Opt in first [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html#opt-in-first)

A baseline is only for apps adopting Pinstripe late; new apps never set it. The app opts in from its own `composer.json`:

```json
{
    "extra": {
        "pinstripe": {
            "legacy": true
        }
    }
}
```

Every command checks the flag before it reads the baseline. Without it, `pinstripe-baseline` exits 2 and says how to add it. In a monorepo, point the command at another composer.json with `--composer=<path>` (default: `composer.json` in the current working directory).

### Count the baseline [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html#count-the-baseline)

```
vendor/bin/pinstripe-baseline count phpstan-baseline.neon
```

prints how many errors the baseline ignores: the sum of each entry's `count`, 1 when `count` is absent.

### Check against a limit [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html#check-against-a-limit)

```
vendor/bin/pinstripe-baseline check --max=42 phpstan-baseline.neon
```

exits 1 with `baseline grew: N errors, the most allowed is M` when the count is above the limit, 0 otherwise.

### Check against the target branch [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html#check-against-the-target-branch)

To compare with the target branch instead of a fixed number, pass a git ref:

```
vendor/bin/pinstripe-baseline check --against=origin/main phpstan-baseline.neon
```

In GitLab CI the merge request's base SHA is already in the environment:

```
vendor/bin/pinstripe-baseline check --against=$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA phpstan-baseline.neon
```

### The policy [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html#the-policy)

An existing app may generate a baseline once with `phpstan analyse --generate-baseline` and include it in its `phpstan.neon`; new code gets no baseline. The count a baseline holds is the sum of each entry's `count`, 1 when `count` is absent, and `pinstripe-baseline count` prints it. `bin/pinstripe-baseline check` fails the build (exit 1) when the baseline grows, either against a fixed limit with `--max=<n>` or against a git ref with `--against=<git-ref>`; in GitLab CI the merge request's base SHA is already in the environment as `$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA`. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 the baseline grew, 2 usage or baseline problem.

Note

A baseline is a tailor's chalk line, and this command is the tape measure: it fails the build the moment the line gets longer. The policy behind this section is recorded in [the ADR](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/adr/0001-phpstan-level-and-baseline-policy.html).

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html#related)

- [Adopting on an existing app](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html)
- [The strict cut](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html)
- [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [Laravel apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html)

## Laravel apps [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#laravel-apps)

This guide shows how to point a Laravel app at Pinstripe's shared presets for Pint and PHPStan, with the Laravel parts included.

### Install [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#install)

Add Pinstripe and Larastan as dev dependencies:

```
composer config allow-plugins.phpstan/extension-installer true
composer require --dev waynestate/pinstripe:^0.3 larastan/larastan
```

`^0.3` gets you 0.3.1, the current release. If Composer cannot find it yet (Packagist reads the GitHub mirror, which can trail a release), add the canonical repository first, as [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html#add-the-dependency) shows.

Note

Pinstripe loads its PHPStan rules through `phpstan/extension-installer`, and Composer will not ask when it cannot prompt. Pinstripe pulls in `phpstan/extension-installer`, which registers Larastan for you. When Composer asks, allow the plugin (`config.allow-plugins` in your `composer.json`).

If Composer stops because a package your app already locks (often an older PHPStan) does not fit, run the same `composer require` again with `-W`, as Composer suggests, so it may update that package too.

### Configure [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#configure)

Your `phpstan.neon` includes `vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/phpstan/laravel.neon` and nothing else: there is no Larastan line to add, and the scripts point at `vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/laravel.json`.

### The env() rule [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#the-env-rule)

The Laravel preset also rejects `env()` outside `config/`: once the config is cached, `env()` returns null, so read config with `config()` instead. The rule is Larastan's, and `phpstan/laravel.neon` pins it on. The environment is not a hand-me-down: take the config out of the wardrobe.

### Banned calls [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#banned-calls)

Every cut also fails on `eval()`, `extract()`, `var_dump()`, `dd()`, `dump()` and the HTTP client's `withoutVerifying()`, whether you call it as `Http::withoutVerifying()` or partway down a chain, and on the long way round to the same hole, `withOptions(['verify' => false])` (Guzzle's `verify` option set to false, in Laravel or in Guzzle itself). Laravel's own `dd()` and `dump()` methods count as well (`$users->dd()`, `DB::table('users')->dumpRawSql()`, `$request->dump()`, `Http::get($url)->dd()`), under the same identifiers as the functions. So does SQL joined from strings: `DB::select('... id = ' . $id)` and the connection's other calls (`insert()`, `update()`, `delete()`, `statement()`, `scalar()`, `cursor()`, `fromQuery()`) want literal SQL with bindings, and Laravel's own `literal-string` types already hold `DB::raw()`, `DB::unprepared()` and `whereRaw()` and the other raw builder methods to the same rule. The [Banned calls](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html) page says why and what to use instead.

### Proven on Laravel [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#proven-on-laravel)

`composer ci` lints a minimal Laravel 13 app (`tests/fixtures/laravel-app`) with `pint/laravel.json` and analyzes it with `phpstan/laravel.neon` on every run, and fails if the app stops passing. A smaller fixture (`tests/fixtures/laravel`) proves the preset really loads Larastan: it plants an undefined Eloquent property that only Larastan reports, and a clean twin it leaves alone. The combined fixture `tests/fixtures/laravel-vue` is one app tree with both PHP and Vue files, with `resources/js` beside `app/`. `composer ci` lints its PHP side with Pint and PHPStan, and `npm test` lints its Vue side with ESLint and Prettier, on every run, with one planted PHP error and two planted Vue defects that each preset must report.

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#related)

- [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [Require strict types](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-types.html)
- [The strict cut](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html)
- [Adopting on an existing app](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html)
- [Best practices](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html)

Source: https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html

## Raw PHP apps [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html#raw-php-apps)

Point a raw PHP app at the Pinstripe presets: Pint for style, PHPStan at level 8 for analysis.

### Add the dependency [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html#add-the-dependency)

Add Pinstripe as a dev dependency:

```bash
composer config allow-plugins.phpstan/extension-installer true
composer require --dev waynestate/pinstripe:^0.3
```

Pinstripe loads its PHPStan rules through `phpstan/extension-installer`, and Composer will not ask when it cannot prompt. If Composer stops because a package your app already locks (often an older PHPStan) does not fit, run the same `composer require` again with `-W`, as Composer suggests, so it may update that package too.

`^0.3` gets you 0.3.1, the current release, with every [banned call](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html). Packagist reads the GitHub mirror, which can trail a release by a while. If Composer says it cannot find a 0.3 version, point it at the canonical repository first (it asks for your git.wayne.edu sign-in), then run the `composer require` again:

```bash
composer config repositories.pinstripe vcs https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/pinstripe.git
```

The npm package, `@waynestate/pinstripe`, is published by hand after each tag; `npm view @waynestate/pinstripe version` shows where it is. The ESLint and Prettier presets have not changed since 0.1.4, so any version from 0.1.4 up is today's cut.

### Point PHPStan at the raw config [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html#point-phpstan-at-the-raw-config)

`phpstan.neon`:

```neon
includes:
    - vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/phpstan/raw.neon

parameters:
    paths:
        - app
```

### Add Composer scripts [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html#add-composer-scripts)

Add Composer scripts that run on every OS:

```json
{
    "scripts": {
        "lint": "pint --test --config vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/per.json",
        "fix": "pint --config vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/per.json",
        "analyse": "phpstan analyse"
    }
}
```

`composer lint` fails on style. `composer fix` fixes it. Pint's `per` preset is the PER Coding Style, and `tests/fixtures/per` keeps a clean and a messy proof. `composer analyse` runs PHPStan at level 8, with deprecation checks too. Pinstripe ships `phpstan/phpstan-deprecation-rules`, loaded automatically by `phpstan/extension-installer`. Calling a `@deprecated` method fails the build. The tailor flags the old cut before the fabric is retired. It also fails on `eval()`, `extract()`, `var_dump()`, `dd()` and `dump()`, and on TLS checks turned off through curl (`CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER` false, `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST` 0), a stream context (`verify_peer` false) or Guzzle (`'verify' => false`), and on SQL joined from strings through PDO, mysqli or `oci_parse()` (bind the values instead): the [Banned calls](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html) page says why and what to use instead.

### Show Pint findings in the merge request [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html#show-pint-findings-in-the-merge-request)

Add a second script that writes the report to a file:

```json
{
    "scripts": {
        "lint:gitlab": "pint --test --config vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/per.json --format=gitlab > pint-codequality.json"
    }
}
```

Point GitLab at the artifact, and keep it when the job fails, which is exactly when it has something to show:

```yaml
artifacts:
    when: always
    reports:
        codequality: pint-codequality.json
```

`--format=gitlab` writes GitLab's Code Quality JSON and `[]` when the code is clean, and Pinstripe tests both. Chalk marks wash out; these findings stay pinned to the merge request.

### Show PHPStan findings in the merge request [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html#show-phpstan-findings-in-the-merge-request)

PHPStan writes the same report with its own `gitlab` error format:

```json
{
    "scripts": {
        "analyse:gitlab": "phpstan analyse --no-progress --error-format=gitlab > phpstan-codequality.json"
    }
}
```

```yaml
artifacts:
    when: always
    reports:
        codequality: phpstan-codequality.json
```

Each finding carries its identifier (`pinstripe.banned.joinedSql`, `argument.type`) as the check name. Pinstripe tests both sides: the raw preset turns the null bug fixture into a non-empty report and the clean fixture into `[]`.

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html#related)

- [Overview](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/index.html)
- [Require strict types](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-types.html)
- [Laravel apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html)
- [The strict cut](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html)
- [Baselines only shrink](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html)

## Rector [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/rector.html#rector)

This guide shows how to use the Pinstripe Rector preset to modernize code for the PHP version your app already supports.

### Install [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/rector.html#install)

Add Rector as a dev dependency:

```
composer require --dev rector/rector
```

### Configure [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/rector.html#configure)

Create `rector.php` and use the Pinstripe preset, adding only your own paths:

```php
<?php

$base = require __DIR__ . '/vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/rector/base.php';

return $base->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src']);
```

The preset reads the PHP floor from your app's own `composer.json`, so it cannot drift out of step with the version the app actually runs on.

### Laravel upgrade rules [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/rector.html#laravel-upgrade-rules)

The preset turns on Rector's composer-based Laravel sets with `withComposerBased(laravel: true)`. Add `driftingly/rector-laravel` as a dev dependency and the preset applies the Laravel upgrade rules that match your app's installed `laravel/framework` version:

```
composer require --dev driftingly/rector-laravel
```

Without the package the call is a no-op, so an app that does not want Laravel rules sees no change.

### Run [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/rector.html#run)

Check with `vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run` and apply with `vendor/bin/rector process`.

### Proven on fixtures [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/rector.html#proven-on-fixtures)

`composer ci` runs the preset against a modern app (`tests/fixtures/rector-clean`) and an old-style one (`tests/fixtures/rector-old`) on every run, and fails if the clean one changes or the old one is left alone. Rector is the tailor's press: it smooths old code to the standard without changing the cut.

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/rector.html#related)

- [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [The strict cut](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html)
- [Adopting on an existing app](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html)
- [Best practices](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html)

Source: https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html

## The strict cut [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html#the-strict-cut)

Point a new app at the strict PHPStan cut so loose comparisons and the strict rules fail the build.

### Choose the strict cut [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html#choose-the-strict-cut)

New apps can include `vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/phpstan/strict.neon` instead of `raw.neon` or `laravel.neon`. It keeps the base cut and turns on `phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules`, so loose comparisons like `==` fail the build. Existing apps stay on the base cut and baseline their way over.

### What the strict cut adds [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html#what-the-strict-cut-adds)

PHPStan checks phpdoc method signatures from level 3 up, and `phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules` forces the two switches behind them on for every run it is installed for. The base cut pins `reportMaybesInMethodSignatures` and `reportStaticMethodSignatures` off so it stays exactly as documented; the strict cut keeps them on, so it also reports maybe-mismatched overrides and static method overrides.

### The eight extra switches [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html#the-eight-extra-switches)

`phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules` forces eight more switches on for every run as well. Each one is decided below: low noise and real bugs stay on in every cut, noisy ones are pinned off in the base cut and turned on only in `strict.neon`.

| Parameter | Raw and Laravel cuts | Strict cut | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checkExplicitMixedMissingReturn` | on | on | A function declared to return `mixed` that can fall off the end is a real bug, and rare in practice. |
| `checkFunctionNameCase` | on | on | A wrongly cased function name works on Windows and macOS and breaks on Linux. |
| `checkInternalClassCaseSensitivity` | on | on | The same case bug for PHP's own classes. |
| `checkStrictPrintfPlaceholderTypes` | on | on | `%d` fed a string is a real formatting bug, and rare. |
| `checkDynamicProperties` | off | on | Floods legacy code with undeclared properties. |
| `reportMaybesInPropertyPhpDocTypes` | off | on | Reports "maybe" phpdoc mismatches that legacy docblocks trip constantly. |
| `reportWrongPhpDocTypeInVarTag` | off | on | Old `@var` tags are often loose; fixing them is cleanup, not bug hunting. |
| `reportNonIntStringArrayKey` | off | on | Bleeding-edge check that is noisy on loosely keyed arrays. |

Note

Strict is the tailor's chalk line drawn before the first stitch.

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html#related)

- [Adopting on an existing app](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html)
- [Baselines only shrink](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html)
- [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [Laravel apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html)
- [ADR-0001: PHPStan level 8 and baselines](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/adr/0001-phpstan-level-and-baseline-policy.html)

## Require strict types [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-types.html#require-strict-types)

Opt in to `declare(strict_types=1)` so every file Pint touches carries the declaration.

### Point the scripts at the strict preset [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-types.html#point-the-scripts-at-the-strict-preset)

Opt-in. Point `composer lint` and `composer fix` at the strict preset instead of `per.json`:

```json
{
    "scripts": {
        "lint": "pint --test --config vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/per-strict.json",
        "fix": "pint --config vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/per-strict.json"
    }
}
```

Warning

`composer fix` adds `declare(strict_types=1);` to every file it touches, so run your tests first and commit the change on its own.

For a big app, Rector's `SafeDeclareStrictTypesRector` is the careful route. Strict types leave no loose threads.

### Covered by tests [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-types.html#covered-by-tests)

Pinstripe runs the real Pint against clean and missing fixtures for `pint/per-strict.json` and `pint/laravel-strict.json`, and asserts each strict config declares its preset and the `declare_strict_types` rule.

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-types.html#related)

- [Overview](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/index.html)
- [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [Laravel apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html)
- [Rector](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/rector.html)

## Vue [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html#vue)

This guide shows how to point a Vue app at Pinstripe's ESLint and Prettier presets.

### Install [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html#install)

Add Pinstripe as a dev dependency:

```
npm install --save-dev @waynestate/pinstripe eslint prettier
```

### Configure ESLint [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html#configure-eslint)

Create `eslint.config.js` and spread the preset. For TypeScript:

```js
import pinstripe from '@waynestate/pinstripe/eslint/typescript'

export default [...pinstripe]
```

For plain JavaScript, import `@waynestate/pinstripe/eslint/javascript` instead.

### Configure Prettier [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html#configure-prettier)

Point Prettier at the preset in `package.json`:

```json
{
    "prettier": "@waynestate/pinstripe/prettier"
}
```

### Add scripts [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html#add-scripts)

Add scripts that run on every OS:

```json
{
    "scripts": {
        "lint": "eslint .",
        "format": "prettier --write ."
    }
}
```

`npm run lint` fails on style and accessibility, and on every Vue and accessibility finding: where the plugins' recommended configs report a rule as a warning, Pinstripe reports it as an error, so the editor, a local run and CI all agree on what fails. `npm run format` fixes the layout.

An app that cannot fix every finding in one cut can spread the `-warn` twin for a while (`@waynestate/pinstripe/eslint/javascript-warn` or `@waynestate/pinstripe/eslint/typescript-warn`): the same rules with the plugins' original severities, so findings that were warnings stay warnings. Switch back to the strict preset once the codebase is clean. The preset is the off-the-rack suit: it fits every app, and you only add your own cufflinks.

Note

If an app adopts Oxlint for speed, ESLint stays in the toolchain for `.vue` files, because Pinstripe's Vue and accessibility rules (eslint-plugin-vue and eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility) run only in ESLint.

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html#related)

- [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [The strict cut](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/strict-cut.html)
- [Best practices](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html)

Source: https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/

## Overview [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#overview)

This page summarizes what Pinstripe is, shows the install and run commands, and points you to the guide for your stack.

### What Pinstripe is [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#what-pinstripe-is)

**Sharp code. Every line.**

The coding standard for the Wayne State app stack: shared presets for Pint, PHPStan (with Larastan for Laravel), Rector, and ESLint with Prettier. Your app points at them and adds only its own exceptions. Pinstripe is to code what a good suit is to a job interview: nobody notices it, everybody notices when it's missing.

It needs PHP ^8.3, runs PHPStan at level 8, and is MIT licensed. Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

Note

**Not to be confused with:** Pinstripe is the code style settings you run locally; Preflight runs them, and PROCTOR, in CI. Pinstripe's Rector set modernizes code within the app's current PHP version, while Booster upgrades the app to a newer PHP version.

### Install and run [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#install-and-run)

In your app, add Pinstripe as a dev dependency, then run the checks:

```bash
composer config allow-plugins.phpstan/extension-installer true
composer require --dev waynestate/pinstripe:^0.3
composer lint
composer fix
composer analyse
```

`composer lint` fails on style. `composer fix` fixes it. `composer analyse` runs PHPStan at level 8, with deprecation checks too.

### Pick your path [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#pick-your-path)

- [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html): point PHPStan at the raw config and Pint at the `per` preset.
- [Laravel apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html): the Laravel preset, with Larastan registered for you.
- [Vue](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/vue.html): the ESLint and Prettier presets for JavaScript, TypeScript and Vue.
- [Rector](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/rector.html): modernize code for the PHP version your app already supports.
- [Tested with](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/tested-with.html): the tool versions Pinstripe is tested with, and the floors each tool needs.

### Status [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#status)

The repository is at version 0.3.1: every cut bans SQL joined from strings, TLS checks turned off and leftover debug calls ([Banned calls](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html)), and `^0.3` installs it. Packagist reads the GitHub mirror, which can trail a release; the [Raw PHP guide](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html#add-the-dependency) shows the one line that installs it from git.wayne.edu meanwhile. The npm package, `@waynestate/pinstripe`, follows each tag at the same version, published by hand; its ESLint and Prettier presets have not changed since 0.1.4. The canonical repository is on git.wayne.edu; GitHub is a read-only push mirror of it, and Packagist and npm read from it. The agent-ready site ships a plain-text twin for machines: [llms.txt](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt).

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#related)

- [Upgrading](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html)
- [Contributing](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html)
- [Changelog](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html)

Source: https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html

## Banned calls [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html#banned-calls)

This page lists the calls every Pinstripe cut fails the build on, says why each is banned and what to use instead, and shows how to keep one on purpose.

### What is banned [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html#what-is-banned)

Every cut (raw, Laravel and strict) includes `phpstan/disallowed.neon` through `base.neon`. The rules come from [spaze/phpstan-disallowed-calls](https://github.com/spaze/phpstan-disallowed-calls), which Pinstripe requires and `phpstan/extension-installer` loads, so your `phpstan.neon` needs no new line. A `dd()` left in after debugging turns the pipeline red, the same as any other PHPStan error.

The one exception is `curl_setopt()` with a verify option set to false: it needs the option and the value together, which that package cannot match, so Pinstripe ships a small rule of its own (`src/PHPStan/CurlVerifyOffRule.php`), registered in the same file. Its report reads and links like the others.

| Call | Why it is banned | Use instead | OWASP Top 10:2025 | ASVS 5.0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eval()` | Runs a string as PHP, so one untrusted value is remote code execution. | Write the code out, or pick a callable with `match`. | A05 Injection | V1.3.2 |
| `extract()` | Turns array keys into variables, so request data can overwrite any variable in scope. | Read the keys you need by name, or destructure the array. | A05 Injection | V15.3.3 (closest: mass assignment) |
| `var_dump()` | Debug output left in ships paths, config and secrets to the browser. | A PSR-3 logger (`Log::debug()` in Laravel), or Xdebug. | A02 Security Misconfiguration | V13.4.2 |
| `dd()` | Dumps internals to the browser and halts the request in production. | The same. | A02 Security Misconfiguration | V13.4.2 |
| `dump()` | The same leak as `var_dump()`, Symfony and Laravel flavored. | The same. | A02 Security Misconfiguration | V13.4.2 |
| Laravel's `->dd()` and `->dump()` methods | The same leaks, called on a collection, query, request or HTTP response (`$users->dd()`, `->dumpRawSql()`, `Http::get($url)->dd()`). | The same. | A02 Security Misconfiguration | V13.4.2 |
| `withoutVerifying()` | Turns off TLS certificate checks in Laravel's HTTP client (`PendingRequest`), so anyone on the path can read or change the traffic. | Keep verification on; for a private CA, pass its bundle through `withOptions` and the `verify` option. | A02 Security Misconfiguration | V12.3.2 |
| `'verify' => false` | The same hole through Guzzle's `verify` option: Laravel's `withOptions()`, `new Client([...])`, and the options of `request()`, `send()`, `get()`, `post()` and the other verbs. | Set `verify` to the path of the CA bundle, or leave it out. | A02 Security Misconfiguration | V12.3.2 |
| `curl_setopt()` and `curl_setopt_array()` with `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER` false or `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST` 0 | Turns off curl's certificate or host name check in raw PHP. | Keep both on; for a private CA, point `CURLOPT_CAINFO` at its bundle. | A02 Security Misconfiguration | V12.3.2 |
| `stream_context_create()` with `ssl` `verify_peer` or `verify_peer_name` false, or `allow_self_signed` true | Turns off the same checks for `file_get_contents()` and the other stream functions. | Keep them on; for a private CA, set the `ssl` `cafile` option. | A02 Security Misconfiguration | V12.3.2 |
| SQL joined from strings: `PDO::query()`, `prepare()` and `exec()`, mysqli (`query()`, `prepare()`, `mysqli_query()` and the rest), `oci_parse()` and its old alias `ociparse()`, and Laravel's `DB::select()`, `insert()`, `update()`, `delete()`, `statement()`, `scalar()`, `cursor()` and `fromQuery()` | A variable joined into the SQL (`'... id = ' . $id`, `"... {$id}"`, `sprintf()`) lets one untrusted value rewrite the query. | Keep the SQL a literal and bind every value (`?` or `:name` placeholders, `oci_bind_by_name()`). | A05 Injection | V1.2.4 |

The ASVS column names the requirement each ban enforces in [OWASP ASVS 5.0.0](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/tree/v5.0.0/5.0/en). ASVS has no requirement for `extract()` by name; mass assignment (V15.3.3) is the closest.

Each ban has a stable identifier: `pinstripe.banned.eval`, `pinstripe.banned.extract`, `pinstripe.banned.varDump`, `pinstripe.banned.dd`, `pinstripe.banned.dump`, `pinstripe.banned.withoutVerifying`, `pinstripe.banned.verifyFalse`, `pinstripe.banned.curlVerifyOff`, `pinstripe.banned.streamVerifyOff` and `pinstripe.banned.joinedSql`.

### SQL joined from strings [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html#sql-joined-from-strings)

The SQL ban stands on PHPStan's own `literal-string` type, so there is no taint rule to trust: PHPStan already knows which strings are literals. These pass:

```php
$pdo->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?')->execute([$id]);
$pdo->query('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ' . self::TABLE);                  // a class constant is a literal
$sql = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE 1 = 1';
if ($activeOnly) {
    $sql .= ' AND active = 1';                                        // literal onto literal
}
$marks = implode(', ', array_fill(0, count($ids), '?'));             // placeholders from literals
$pdo->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN (' . $marks . ')')->execute($ids);
DB::select('select * from users where id = ?', [$id]);
```

Anything with a variable in it fails, an `int` included (bind it):

```php
$pdo->query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ' . $id);                 // pinstripe.banned.joinedSql
DB::select("select * from users where id = {$id}");                 // pinstripe.banned.joinedSql
```

`ociparse()` is also reported as deprecated (`function.deprecated`) on every PHP version Pinstripe supports, whatever the SQL looks like, and the fix is `oci_parse()`.

Laravel already types `DB::raw()`, `DB::unprepared()` and the query builder's `whereRaw()`, `selectRaw()`, `orderByRaw()` and other raw methods as `literal-string`, so PHPStan reports a joined string there by itself, as `argument.type`; Pinstripe covers the connection calls Laravel leaves as plain `string`. The query builder's own `insert()`, `update()`, `delete()` and `select()` take arrays and column names, not SQL, and are not touched.

SQL that is safe but not a literal (read from a `.sql` file, or returned by a helper) can say so, or the call can keep a reasoned ignore.

#### SQL kept in .sql files [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html#sql-kept-in-sql-files)

Many apps keep their queries in `.sql` files and bind every value. That is safe, but PHPStan cannot tell that a file's contents are static, so the ban reports every call that runs one. It is the report older Wayne State apps meet most often. One typed reader clears all of them, with the one reasoned ignore in one place:

```php
/**
 * @param literal-string $name
 *
 * @return literal-string
 */
function sqlFile(string $name): string
{
    $sql = file_get_contents(__DIR__ . '/sql/' . $name . '.sql');
    if ($sql === false) {
        throw new RuntimeException('No such query: ' . $name);
    }

    // @phpstan-ignore return.type (the SQL is read from the app's own sql/ folder, and every value is bound)
    return $sql;
}

$statement = oci_parse($oracle, sqlFile('people'));
oci_bind_by_name($statement, ':id', $id);
```

The name is `literal-string` too, so a request value can never pick the file. A helper that only ever returns literals needs no ignore at all: type it `@return literal-string` and PHPStan checks that it is true.

#### Type a wrapper, never baseline it [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html#type-a-wrapper-never-baseline-it)

A wrapper that takes the whole SQL as a plain `string` is reported once, inside the wrapper, and never at its callers:

```php
function query($db, string $sql)
{
    return oci_parse($db, $sql); // pinstripe.banned.joinedSql, here and only here
}
```

Baseline that one line and every caller, today's and every one written after it, goes unchecked for good. Type the parameter instead:

```php
/**
 * @param resource $db
 * @param literal-string $sql
 */
function query($db, string $sql)
{
    return oci_parse($db, $sql);
}
```

Now PHPStan checks each caller: literal SQL passes, and a joined string is reported where it is joined, as `argument.type` ("expects literal-string").

#### Other ways out [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html#other-ways-out)

- Give PHPStan the connection's type, a typed property or `@var \PDO $db`; with a `mixed` connection PHPStan cannot see the call, and the ban stays quiet.
- An older app with many joined queries can baseline the rest while it binds them, since a baseline only shrinks. Baseline call sites, never a wrapper.

Only the off switch is banned: `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER` set to true, `verify` pointed at a CA bundle, and `false` on an option that has nothing to do with TLS all pass. The match is on literal values, so `'verify' => $verify`, or a curl option read from config, passes too; keep the value a literal where you can.

Laravel's methods share the functions' identifiers: `dd()`, `ddRawSql()`, `ddHeaders()`, `ddBody()`, `ddJson()` and `ddSession()` report as `pinstripe.banned.dd`, and `dump()`, `dumpRawSql()`, `dumpHeaders()` and `dumpSession()` as `pinstripe.banned.dump`. Facade calls such as `Http::dd()` count too. Only methods Laravel itself declares are caught, so your own `dump()` method is fine, and so is the schema dump behind `php artisan schema:dump`.

The `withoutVerifying()` ban catches both `Http::withoutVerifying()` and the method partway down a chain such as `Http::acceptJson()->withoutVerifying()`. Raw PHP apps never match it.

A report reads like this (wrapped here), with the reason, the fix and the OWASP tag in one message. Its tip links to this page and to the [CREED rule](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/code.html#banned-patterns):

```text
Calling dd() is forbidden, a dd() left in dumps internals to the browser and halts the request in production;
log it with a PSR-3 logger (Log::debug() in Laravel), or step through with Xdebug (OWASP A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration).
```

### Keep one on purpose [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html#keep-one-on-purpose)

Use the ban's identifier and say why in parentheses, as with any other ignore. Every cut reports an ignore without a reason.

```php
// @phpstan-ignore pinstripe.banned.varDump (CLI-only diagnostics; output goes to the operator's terminal)
var_dump($report);
```

On an existing app, fix the banned calls rather than baselining them: each is usually one line, and a baseline would hide the next one too.

### Add your own [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html#add-your-own)

List more bans under the same parameters (`disallowedFunctionCalls`, `disallowedMethodCalls`, `disallowedStaticCalls`) in your app's `phpstan.neon`. NEON appends lists, so yours join Pinstripe's. The package's [custom rules guide](https://github.com/spaze/phpstan-disallowed-calls/blob/main/docs/custom-rules.md) shows every key.

### Not covered yet [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html#not-covered-yet)

- An off switch PHPStan cannot pin to a value: `'verify' => $verify`, or a curl option read from config.
- Postgres's `pg_query()` and friends: the connection argument is optional, so the SQL has no fixed position to check.

### Not banned yet [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html#not-banned-yet)

`md5()`, `sha1()`, `rand()` and `mt_rand()` are weak for passwords, tokens and signatures, but they are fine for cache keys, checksums and other non-security uses, and apps across the fleet use them that way. Whether Pinstripe bans them (and how it would allow the safe uses) is an open call, so for now they pass.

### How it is proven [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html#how-it-is-proven)

`composer ci` runs these on every change:

- `tests/fixtures/raw-disallowed/src/Leftovers.php` makes each banned call once, and the raw and strict cuts must report each one, by identifier, with its OWASP tag, and nothing else.
- Its clean twin, `LookAlikes.php`, defines methods named `dump()` and `dd()` and uses `var_export()` and `match`, and must stay green; `Excused.php` keeps one `var_dump()` with a reasoned ignore and must stay green too.
- `tests/fixtures/laravel/src/LeftoverDebugMethods.php` leaves seven of Laravel's `dd()` and `dump()` methods in (on a collection, a query, a request, an HTTP response and the `Http` facade), and the Laravel preset must report each one; its twin `SchemaDump.php` writes a schema dump and must stay green.
- `tests/fixtures/laravel/src/InsecureHttp.php` turns TLS checks off both ways, and the Laravel preset must report both.
- `tests/fixtures/raw-disallowed/src/InsecureTransport.php` turns TLS checks off eight ways through curl and stream contexts, and the raw and strict cuts must report each one; its twin `SecureTransport.php` sets verification on and must stay green.
- `tests/fixtures/laravel/src/VerifyFalse.php` sets `verify` to false five ways through `withOptions()` and Guzzle, and the Laravel preset must report each one; its twin `VerifiedHttp.php` points `verify` at a CA bundle and must stay green.
- `tests/fixtures/raw-disallowed/src/JoinedSql.php` joins a variable into SQL nine ways through PDO, mysqli, `oci_parse()` and its old alias `ociparse()`, and the raw and strict cuts must report each one; its twin `BoundSql.php` binds every value and must stay green.
- `tests/fixtures/raw-disallowed/src/SqlFiles.php` reads its SQL from `.sql` files through the typed reader and wrapper above and must stay green in the raw and strict cuts; `JoinedThroughAWrapper.php` hands joined SQL to that wrapper and must be reported at each caller, while a plain-`string` wrapper is reported once, inside, and its joined caller not at all.
- `tests/fixtures/laravel/src/JoinedQueries.php` does the same six ways through Laravel's connection and three through the raw builder methods, and the Laravel preset must report all nine (six as `pinstripe.banned.joinedSql`, three as Laravel's own `argument.type`); its twin `BoundQueries.php` uses bindings and the query builder and must stay green.
- The Laravel app fixture installs Pinstripe through Composer, like an app does, and must fail on a leftover `dd()`, and on curl told to skip the certificate check (which proves Pinstripe's own curl rule loads from `vendor/`).

A suit with a `dd()` in the pocket does not leave the shop.

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html#related)

- [Laravel apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html)

## Best practices [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#best-practices)

This page lists every rule Pinstripe holds itself to and the tests that prove each one. It carries BEST_PRACTICES.md word for word, and `BestPracticesTest` fails the build when the two drift apart.

How Pinstripe keeps its own promises: every preset is enforced by a test that runs the real tool against a fixture, so a preset that stops working fails `composer ci` here instead of failing a developer's app. A preset without a test is a suit without a mirror: you cannot tell when it has gone wrinkled.

A preset is **Enforced** when a test asserts both directions: a clean fixture passes, and a deliberately broken one is caught. It is **Checked** when a test runs the real tool in one direction only: the clean side passes, or the broken side is caught, but not both yet. The PHP presets run under `composer ci` (PHPUnit); the JavaScript presets run under `npm test`. Both run in CI on GitLab and GitHub, so a preset that stops working fails the pipeline before it reaches an app.

| Preset | Tool | Status | Enforced by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pint/per.json` | Pint | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testPintPerPresetAcceptsTheCleanFixture`, `PresetsTest::testPintPerPresetRejectsTheMessyFixture` |
| `Pint GitLab output` | Pint | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testPintGitlabFormatReportsTheMessyFixtureAsCodeQualityJson`, `PresetsTest::testPintGitlabFormatIsAnEmptyArrayForTheCleanFixture` |
| `PHPStan GitLab output` | PHPStan | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testPhpStanGitlabFormatReportsTheNullBugAsCodeQualityJson`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanGitlabFormatIsAnEmptyArrayForTheCleanFixture` |
| `ESLint GitLab output` | ESLint | Enforced | `tests/js/gitlab-formatter.test.mjs` (`npm test`: the bad fixture gives findings, the clean one an empty report) |
| `pint/laravel.json` | Pint | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testPintLaravelPresetAcceptsTheLaravelAppFixture`, `PresetsTest::testPintLaravelPresetRejectsTheMessyFixture` |
| `pint/per-strict.json` | Pint | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testPintPerStrictPresetAcceptsTheStrictTypesCleanFixture`, `PresetsTest::testPintPerStrictPresetRejectsTheStrictTypesMissingFixture` |
| `pint/laravel-strict.json` | Pint | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testPintLaravelStrictPresetAcceptsTheStrictTypesLaravelCleanFixture`, `PresetsTest::testPintLaravelStrictPresetRejectsTheStrictTypesMissingFixture` |
| `phpstan/raw.neon` | PHPStan | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testPhpStanRawConfigAcceptsTheCleanFixture`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanRawConfigReportsTheNullBug` |
| `phpstan/strict.neon` | PHPStan + strict-rules | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testPhpStanStrictConfigAcceptsTheCleanFixture`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanStrictConfigReportsTheLooseComparison` |
| `phpstan/disallowed.neon` (banned calls) | PHPStan + disallowed-calls | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testPhpStanReportsEveryBannedCall`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanAcceptsMethodsThatShareTheBannedNames`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanRawConfigAcceptsABannedCallKeptWithAReason`, `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetReportsTlsVerificationTurnedOff` |
| `phpstan/laravel.neon` | PHPStan + Larastan | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetLoadsLarastanThroughTheExtensionInstaller`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanLaravelConfigAcceptsTheLaravelAppFixture`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanLaravelConfigReportsTheUndefinedEloquentProperty` |
| `Larastan env() rule` | PHPStan + Larastan | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetReportsAnEnvCallOutsideConfig`, `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetAcceptsAConfigCallOutsideConfig` |
| `PHPStan ignore comments` | PHPStan | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testPhpStanRawConfigReportsAnIgnoreWithoutAComment`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanRawConfigReportsAnIgnoreThatMatchesNothing`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanRawConfigAcceptsAnIgnoreWithAComment` |
| `Laravel dd() and dump() methods banned` | PHPStan + Larastan | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetReportsDdAndDumpMethodsLeftIn`, `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetAcceptsASchemaDump` |
| `TLS checks turned off banned` | PHPStan (+ Pinstripe's curl rule) | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testPhpStanReportsTlsChecksTurnedOffInRawPhp`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanAcceptsTlsChecksLeftOnInRawPhp`, `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetReportsTheVerifyOptionSetToFalse`, `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetAcceptsVerifyPointedAtACaBundle`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanLaravelConfigReportsCurlVerifyOffInTheLaravelAppFixture` |
| `SQL joined from strings banned` | PHPStan (`literal-string`) + disallowed-calls | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testPhpStanReportsSqlJoinedFromStringsInRawPhp`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanAcceptsLiteralSqlWithBoundValuesInRawPhp`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanAcceptsSqlReadFromFilesThroughATypedWrapper`, `PresetsTest::testPhpStanReportsSqlJoinedThroughAWrapperAtTheCaller`, `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetReportsSqlJoinedFromStrings`, `PresetsTest::testLaravelPresetAcceptsLiteralSqlWithBindings` |
| `Banned call tips link to the CREED rule` | PHPStan | Enforced | `tests/BannedCallLinksTest.php` (`BannedCallLinksTest::testEveryBanCarriesAnIdentifierAndATip` makes sure no entry goes without) |
| `rector/base.php` | Rector | Enforced | `PresetsTest::testRectorPresetAcceptsTheCleanFixture`, `PresetsTest::testRectorPresetReportsChangesOnTheOldFixture` |
| `eslint/javascript.js` | ESLint | Enforced | `tests/js/presets.test.mjs` (`npm test`) |
| `eslint/typescript.js` | ESLint | Enforced | `tests/js/presets.test.mjs` (`npm test`) |
| `prettier/index.json` | Prettier | Enforced | `tests/js/prettier.test.mjs` (`npm test`) |
| README "Tool floors" | composer.lock + package-lock.json | Enforced | `ToolFloorsTest::testToolFloorsMatchTheLockFiles` |
| This page | PHPUnit | Enforced | `BestPracticesTest::testEveryTestNamedHereExists`, `BestPracticesTest::testEveryFileNamedHereExists`, `BestPracticesTest::testEveryRowHasAKnownStatusAndAnEnforcedRowNamesItsTests`, `BestPracticesTest::testTheDocsPageCarriesTheSameTable`, `BestPracticesTest::testTheTallyCountsTheTable` |

Tally: 23 rows, 23 Enforced, 0 Checked.

## Proof [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#proof)

This page says how Pinstripe was proven on real Wayne State applications: what ran, what held, what the run caught in Pinstripe itself, and what it does not prove yet. Next, see [Adopting on an existing app](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html) for the path the run followed and [Baselines only shrink](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html) for the baseline rules.

A suit is proven at the fitting, not on the hanger. So on 2026-11-05 the presets were fitted to every PHP application in the stack's shared proof corpus, the same set PROCTOR, Squire and Preflight are measured on.

### Last run [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#last-run)

| Check | Date | Commit | Result | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `composer ci` (all five) | 2026-11-07 | bf8a2c3 | pass: 67 tests, 382 assertions, 1 skipped, exit 0 | 744 s |
| `composer validate --strict` | 2026-11-07 | bf8a2c3 | pass: composer.json is valid | under 1 s |
| `php bin/agent-ready.php --check` | 2026-11-07 | bf8a2c3 | pass: 22 agent-ready files current | 1 s |
| `composer audit` | 2026-11-07 | bf8a2c3 | pass: no security vulnerability advisories found | 1 s |
| `php bin/docs-site.php --check` | 2026-11-07 | bf8a2c3 | pass: 17 docs pages current | 3 s |

To refresh this table, regenerate the site with `composer docs` and `composer site:agent-ready`, rerun `composer ci`, and rewrite the rows with the new counts and the commit you ran on. The 82-application proof run described below did not run here: its corpus of internal application repositories is not reachable from this machine, and the npm side (ESLint and Prettier for Vue) runs in the npm-test CI job, not in `composer ci`.

### What ran [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-ran)

Pinstripe 0.1.3, the presets as they are on `main`, with PHP 8.4. The 82 applications are 64 raw PHP apps (33 with a `composer.json`, 31 without one), 17 Laravel apps from 5.8 to 13, and 1 Slim 2 app. Laravel apps got the `laravel` presets; every other app got `per` and `raw`.

Each app was a throwaway copy of its default branch, checked out with Linux line endings, with `.env` files, `auth.json` and `config.files/` removed. Packagist was reachable; every Wayne State host was mapped to `127.0.0.1`, so nothing private could be fetched. Then, for each app:

1. Pint in test mode with the shape's preset, on the whole app, with a 15 minute limit;
2. for an app with a `composer.json`, the install the README gives: `composer require --dev waynestate/pinstripe:^0.1`, plus `larastan/larastan` for Laravel, and once more with `-W` when Composer itself said a locked package was in the way;
3. PHPStan with the preset: inside the app when the install worked, and otherwise, for a raw app, from a separate Pinstripe install pointed at the app's files;
4. where the install worked and PHPStan found errors: a baseline generated with `--generate-baseline`, PHPStan run again with it, and `pinstripe-baseline count` on it.

An app **passes** when Pint and PHPStan are both clean. It is **flagged** when either reports findings, or when the install could not finish for a reason the app owns. A **tool error** is a crash, a timeout, a report that is not valid, or a Pinstripe command that does not do what it says.

### Results [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#results)

| Units | Pass | Flagged | Tool error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 82 applications | 0 | 81 | 1 |

No application was clean on day one, which is what a coding standard adopted late looks like. The tool error is a Pint timeout, described below.

| Step | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| Pint | Ran on all 82 apps and finished on 81, every one with findings: a median of 14 files to restyle, at most 180. The median app took 2 seconds. |
| Install | 12 of the 51 apps with a `composer.json` installed Pinstripe, one of them only with `-W`. The other 39 stopped on the app's own dependencies: 36 install a package from a private Git repository that the run could not reach, 2 need a PHP extension the run did not have, and for 1 Composer refused the update because the app's locked framework has security advisories. |
| PHPStan | Ran on 66 apps (12 inside the app, 54 raw apps from the separate install) and finished on all 66 with errors at level 8: a median of 86, at most 6,721. No crash, no memory limit hit. The median app took 11 seconds. The 16 Laravel apps that could not install were not analysed, because Larastan needs the app's own framework. |
| Baselines | Generated on all 12 apps that installed. With the baseline, PHPStan was green on 10. On the other 2 PHPStan said some errors could not be put into a baseline (classes that extend a class it could not find). `pinstripe-baseline count` read every baseline, and its count plus the errors PHPStan could not baseline equals PHPStan's total on every app. |

### What it caught in Pinstripe [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-it-caught-in-pinstripe)

A run that only finds praise was not looking hard enough. This one found these, and every finding is about Pinstripe, not the apps:

- **Fixed: `pinstripe-baseline count` printed an app's deprecations.** Installed in an app, the command loads the app's autoloader, and one app's old HTTP library printed PHP 8.4 deprecations ahead of the count. A script reading the number got a page of warnings. The command now mutes deprecations while it loads the autoloader, and a test covers it.
- **Documented: `-W`.** The install line failed on an app that already locked an older PHPStan, and Composer's own advice, `-W`, fixed it. The README and the guides now say so.
- **Documented: what a baseline cannot hold.** [Adopting on an existing app](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html) now says what to do when PHPStan cannot baseline an error, and how to keep Pint off a library the app bundles.
- **Open: Pint on bundled libraries.** One app bundles a PDF library whose generated font maps are single arrays hundreds of kilobytes long. Pint spent over 100 seconds on one such file and did not finish the app in 15 minutes. That is Pint's fixer, not Pinstripe's preset, and the guide's advice is to point Pint at your own folders.
- **Open: Laravel apps that cannot install.** Larastan analyses a Laravel app through its framework, so an app whose dependencies cannot install gets no PHPStan result at all, while a raw app still gets one from a separate install.

### What this does not prove [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-this-does-not-prove)

- No app adopted Pinstripe for real: nothing was committed, and the restyling Pint proposed was not applied or reviewed.
- No private package could be fetched, so 36 apps never got past the install, and 16 Laravel apps were not analysed.
- The npm side (ESLint and Prettier for Vue) did not run here.
- The per-app record names the applications and stays in the stack's internal notes.

### Run it on your app [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#run-it-on-your-app)

The same steps on your own app, from its root:

```sh
composer config allow-plugins.phpstan/extension-installer true
composer require --dev waynestate/pinstripe:^0.3
vendor/bin/pint --test --config vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/per.json
vendor/bin/phpstan analyse
```

For a Laravel app, add `larastan/larastan` to the `require` line and use `pint/laravel.json`. Then follow [Adopting on an existing app](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html) to baseline what is there and keep the new code clean.

### Related [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#related)

- [Adopting on an existing app](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/adopting.html)
- [Baselines only shrink](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/baselines.html)
- [Raw PHP apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [Laravel apps](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html)

## Tested with and tool floors [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/tested-with.html#tested-with-and-tool-floors)

This page records the tool versions Pinstripe is tested with and the PHP or Node floor each locked tool declares.

### Tested with [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/tested-with.html#tested-with)

- Pint 1.32.1
- PHPStan 2.3.3
- PHPStan extension-installer 1.4.3
- PHPStan strict-rules 2.1.0
- Larastan 3.13.2
- Rector 2.8.2
- PHPStan disallowed-calls 4.15.0
- ESLint 10.13.0
- Prettier 3.9.10
- eslint-plugin-vue 10.12.0
- eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility 2.6.3
- typescript-eslint 8.72.1
- Node 22, 24 and 26 (the JS presets run in CI on all three; the floor stays 22.13)

### Tool floors [#](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/tested-with.html#tool-floors)

Can your app run Pinstripe's tools? Each row shows the floor the locked package itself declares, read verbatim from `composer.lock` and `package-lock.json` today and checked against them by `tests/ToolFloorsTest.php`, so a dependency bump forces a README update in the same change.

PHP tools:

| Tool | Locked version | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `laravel/pint` | v1.32.1 | `^8.3.0` |
| `phpstan/phpstan` | 2.3.3 | `^7.4\|^8.0` |
| `phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules` | 2.1.0 | `^7.4 \|\| ^8.0` |
| `phpstan/phpstan-deprecation-rules` | 2.0.5 | `^7.4 \|\| ^8.0` |
| `larastan/larastan` | v3.13.2 | `^8.2` |
| `rector/rector` | 2.8.2 | `^7.4\|^8.0` |
| `spaze/phpstan-disallowed-calls` | v4.15.0 | `^7.4 \|\| ^8.0` |

Node tools:

| Tool | Locked version | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eslint` | 10.13.0 | `^20.19.0 \|\| ^22.13.0 \|\| >=24` |
| `eslint-plugin-vue` | 10.12.0 | `^18.18.0 \|\| ^20.9.0 \|\| >=21.1.0` |
| `typescript-eslint` | 8.72.1 | `^18.18.0 \|\| ^20.9.0 \|\| >=21.1.0` |
| `prettier` | 3.9.10 | `>=14` |

- Pinstripe itself needs PHP 8.3 or newer and Node 22.13 or newer, so the Pint floor is the binding PHP floor.
- Pint only reads and rewrites files, so an app still on an older PHP can run Pint with a PHP 8.3 or newer binary (for example a container) while the app itself keeps its runtime.
- ESLint 10 is what sets the Node floor: Node 20 before 20.19 is out.

Measure twice, cut once: these floors are cut from the lock files, and the test keeps the hem honest.
